plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers, prized in temperate gardens. Many cultivars have single, semi-double, or fully double blooms that stand out against winter landscapes.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring, peaking in midwinter in mild climates
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant from which all true tea is made, and camellias are the state flower of Alabama.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing perennial with nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that age to pinkish tones. It thrives in cool, shaded woodland conditions and blooms when little else does, even pushing through snow.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter to early spring in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the mountains of Central and Southern Europe; grown in gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a rose at all but a member of the buttercup family, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A striking shrub with the largest flower head of any protea, made up of a central cone surrounded by showy, petal-like bracts. It is adapted to fire-prone, nutrient-poor fynbos habitats.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak flowering from December to February in some regions
plants.location: Native to the Western and Eastern Cape of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: It is the national flower of South Africa, and its genus is named after the Greek god Proteus because of its many forms.

plants.name: Hippeastrum hybrids
plants.description: A bulbous plant producing tall, sturdy stalks topped with several huge trumpet-shaped flowers. It is widely forced into bloom indoors in the Northern Hemisphere during winter and blooms outdoors in tropical regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter indoors in the Northern Hemisphere; spring to summer outdoors in native ranges
plants.location: Native to tropical and subtropical South America; popular as a potted houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: A single bulb can bloom again for decades if it is given a dormant rest period and proper feeding each year.
